mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when labor market indicators are strong.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is above 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS rising above its 5-year moving average for four consecutive months) signals elevated precautionary behavior by households, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 250,000 new jobs for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage inflation and cost pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 250000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 0.4% signals a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -0.4% AND HOUST falls > -0.4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.
